title: How the 'Three Ts' System Worked
grammar: Institutional classification with impersonal active 3rd plural (kategóriába sorolják / tekintik)
goal: I can explain how György Aczél's 'three Ts' (támogatott, tűrt, tiltott) cultural policy worked in Kádár-era Hungary.
I can use agentless 3rd person plural active verbs to describe institutional classification and societal norms.
I can talk about censorship, state subsidies and the unwritten limits of what could be said.

sections.title: The Three Ts: Censorship, Aczél's Cultural Policy & Samizdat
body: After the 1956 revolution was put down, the Kádár regime developed a distinctive form of cultural control. Steered by the party's cultural-policy chief György Aczél, the state moved from crude Stalinist terror to the policy usually summed up as the 'Three Ts': Támogatott (Supported), Tűrt (Tolerated), and Tiltott (Prohibited). Instead of rigid rules, ambiguity reigned, prompting artists to internalize self-censorship or invent elaborate allegorical codes.

In this unit, you will explore the secret bargains between censors and creators, decode the 'flower language' (virágnyelv) of Hungarian theatre and literature, visit clandestine stencil printshops in private apartments, and examine how the underground samizdat journal Beszélő prepared the ground for democratic transition. Grammatically, you will revisit the agent-backgrounding structures from B2 Unit 15 (institutional 3rd plural, -ra/-re kerül, middle-voice verbs) and add evaluative predicates with -nak/-nek.
